workflow:
# Building UI with Nucleux

Nucleux (`@nucleux/react`) is a React + Tailwind design system in two families:
shadcn-style (`Button`, `Disclosure`, …) and Material 3 (`Md3Button`,
`Md3Disclosure`, …). The `nucleux` MCP server holds its curated page patterns and
exact component contracts. Work design-first: find the pattern, read the
contracts, then write code.

## Rules

1. Inspect the project before changing files. Keep its framework, router,
   state management, business logic and file layout.
2. Look for a Nucleux pattern (`search_patterns`) before laying out any page.
   Prefer a whole pattern over assembling unrelated components.
3. Read the contract (`get_component`) before using a component. Use only the
   imports, props and variant values it lists. Never guess a Nucleux export,
   prop or variant. If it is not in the catalog, it does not exist.
4. Pick one family per app and do not mix them: Material 3 (`Md3*`) when the
   project already uses Material Design or the user asks for it, otherwise
   shadcn. Patterns are written with shadcn components; in a Material 3 app use
   each one's `Md3` twin, and where Material 3 has none (e.g. `DataTable`), the
   shadcn component under the `md3-theme` class. Agentic components have the
   same props in both families.
5. For AI features use the agentic components (nucleux.in's patterns):
   `Disclosure` and `Caveat` for AI output, `Consent` before acting,
   `OpenInput`/`InitialCta`/`SuggestedPrompts` for asking, the Prompt Scaffolds
   (`Suggestions`, `Madlibs`, `PromptEnhancer`, `Modes`, `VoiceTone`,
   `PresetStyles`) for shaping a request beside the composer, `Attachments`,
   `VoiceInput` and friends for input, `ModelSelection`, `KnowledgeBase`,
   `Connector` and `McpConnection` for context. Search for them with
   `search_components` instead of building your own.
6. Do not rebuild something Nucleux already ships (navigation, tables, cards,
   dialogs, sheets, form controls, empty/error states). If you must, say why
   in your summary.
7. Style with the semantic token classes (`bg-background`, `text-foreground`,
   `text-muted-foreground`, `border-border`, `bg-primary`, `text-destructive`…;
   in a Material 3 app the `md-*` roles: `bg-md-surface`, `text-md-on-surface`,
   `bg-md-primary-container`…).
   No hex colors, no arbitrary color values. Use the same variant for the same
   meaning everywhere (one `cta` primary action per page, `destructive` only
   for destructive actions).
8. Every page must work from 360px wide: follow each pattern's responsive rules.
9. Accessibility is part of done: labels for every control, `aria-label` on
   icon-only buttons, visible focus, status not conveyed by color alone.
10. Every data view handles loading, empty and error (the `page-states` pattern).
11. When Nucleux has no pattern or component for a need, build it from Nucleux
   primitives (or the ShadCN equivalent the tools name), keep it on Nucleux
   tokens, and report the gap. Never present an invented component as Nucleux.
12. Nucleux is not mandatory. If the project already uses another component
    system and the user did not ask to switch, extend that system and say so.

## Workflow

**A. Inspect the project.** Find the framework (Vite, Next.js, Remix…), package
manager (lockfile), TypeScript, Tailwind version and config, router, existing
component system, and any installed `@nucleux/*` packages. If Nucleux is not set
up, call `get_setup` and follow it exactly.

**B. Analyse the request.** List the pages, the main user journeys, the key
interactions on each page, and what matters most on each screen. Ask only about
ambiguities that change the architecture; pick sensible defaults otherwise.

**C. Discover.** For each page call `search_patterns` with what the page is for,
then `get_pattern` for the best match (`app-shell` for the frame, plus one
pattern per page). Call `get_component` for every component you will use that
you have not read in this session. Use `search_components` for needs inside a
page that no pattern covers.

**D. Plan.** Write a short plan: shared layout, then each route →
pattern(s) → components → app-specific pieces you will write → states. Mark
anything Nucleux does not cover. Check the plan with `validate_design` (pattern
ids plus the components and props you intend to use) and fix every error.

**E. Implement.** Build the shared shell once and wrap every route in it.
Start each page from its pattern's example, replace the sample data with the
app's data model, and keep app-specific components (a TaskCard bound to your
data) in the app, composed from Nucleux parts.

**F. Validate.** Run the project's type check, lint, tests and production build;
fix every error. Re-check each page against its pattern's responsive and
accessibility rules.

**G. Report.** Summarise the pages built, the patterns and components used per
page, design decisions, the checks you ran and their results, anything you built
custom and why, and the gaps or open issues.

patterns.name: Analytics with charts
patterns.summary: Range filter in the header and a responsive grid of chart cards built with ChartContainer (Recharts), token colors, tooltip, legend and a screen-reader summary.
patterns.description: Trend and breakdown charts for an analytics page or a dashboard section. ChartContainer maps each series in a ChartConfig to a --color-<key> CSS variable, so series colors come from Nucleux tokens and switch with the theme.
whenToUse: Showing change over time or comparisons across categories.
whenNotToUse: A few headline numbers: use MetricCard tiles from dashboard-overview.
Exact values users need to read or export: use a table (list-page).

children.role: Page header: <h1> title + muted description, flex-col sm:flex-row; actions slot holds the range NativeSelect
sr-only text summary of the chart
config + one Recharts chart (LineChart, BarChart…), aria-hidden

layout: One chart per card with a title that says what it measures.
Give ChartContainer an aspect ratio (aspect-[16/9] w-full) so it sizes responsively.
Series fill/stroke use var(--color-<key>) from the ChartConfig.
responsive: Cards stack below lg, two columns from lg.
Fewer x-axis ticks on narrow cards: keep labels short ("Oct 5").
tokens: Series colors: hsl(var(--nx-info)), hsl(var(--nx-success)), hsl(var(--nx-brand)), hsl(var(--nx-warning)), hsl(var(--nx-destructive))
accessibility: Charts are visual only: add an sr-only text summary and mark ChartContainer aria-hidden, or offer a table view.
Don't rely on color alone: use the legend and distinct chart types or dash patterns when series are many.
patterns.states: Loading: Skeleton at the chart's aspect ratio inside the card. No data: Empty inside the card.
antiPatterns: Hex or Tailwind palette colors for series.
Charts without titles or units.
Importing Recharts' Tooltip/Legend instead of ChartTooltip/ChartLegend with the Nucleux content components.

npm.name: recharts
npm.reason: Chart primitives (LineChart, BarChart, XAxis…) rendered inside ChartContainer. Install the version @nucleux/chart depends on (^2.15).

patterns.name: Application shell
patterns.summary: Collapsible sidebar navigation, a top bar with search and account, and a phone navigation sheet around the page content.
patterns.description: The frame every page of a multi-page web app renders inside, built on the shadcn-style Sidebar. On desktop the Sidebar sits beside the page and collapses to icons (with tooltips) via SidebarTrigger or ⌘B / Ctrl+B; below md the same Sidebar opens as a sheet. Build it once and wrap every route in it.
whenToUse: The app has three or more top-level sections the user switches between.
Pages share global search, notifications or an account menu.
whenNotToUse: Single-page tools or landing pages with no section navigation.
Chat-first agent UIs: use the agent-chat example (get_example) instead.
The project already has a working shell: reuse it and only swap inner components.

composition.role: Wraps the whole app layout; owns open state and the ⌘B shortcut

children.role: App name (sr-only when collapsed to icons)
asChild around an <a href>; isActive for the current route; tooltip = label (shown when collapsed)
Edge hit area that toggles the sidebar
type="search" global search, hidden below sm
Page content; each route renders here

layout: SidebarProvider wraps the whole layout once, around the routes; Sidebar and SidebarInset are its direct children.
SidebarInset is the page column: put the top bar and the routed page inside it. Pages own their padding and max width (see list-page, dashboard-overview).
Use collapsible="icon" for apps people work in all day (icons + tooltips when collapsed); "offcanvas" for content sites.
Close the phone sheet after navigating: useSidebar().setOpenMobile(false) when isMobile.
responsive: md and up: Sidebar beside the page; SidebarTrigger collapses it (to icons with collapsible="icon").
Below md: Sidebar renders as a sheet that SidebarTrigger opens; close it after navigating.
Below sm: hide the header search Input (className="hidden sm:block") or move search into the page.
accessibility: Wrap the menu in <nav aria-label="Primary">.
SidebarMenuButton isActive sets aria-current="page"; drive it from the router, not local state.
SidebarTrigger has an accessible name ("Toggle Sidebar"); other icon-only Buttons need aria-label ("Notifications").
When collapsed to icons, every SidebarMenuButton needs tooltip so the label is still visible on hover and focus.
patterns.routing: SidebarMenuButton asChild renders your link. With React Router or TanStack Router pass their <Link>; with a plain <a>, keep href for real URLs and call preventDefault + navigate in onClick. In Next.js pass next/link's <Link>.
antiPatterns: Hand-rolling an <aside> with custom link styles instead of Sidebar/SidebarMenuButton.
Rendering the shell inside each page instead of once around the routes.
A second, separately maintained link list for phones (the Sidebar already becomes a sheet).
Icon-only collapsed items without tooltip.

npm.name: lucide-react
npm.reason: Icons in the example. Any icon set works.

patterns.name: Sign-in screen
patterns.summary: Centered card with email and password, inline field errors, a form-level error Alert, remember-me, and links to reset password and sign up.
patterns.description: The authentication entry point. One focused card on a muted background; validation runs on submit and marks each invalid field; a failed sign-in shows a destructive Alert above the fields and keeps what the user typed. Sign-up and password reset reuse the same card layout with different fields.
whenToUse: Email/password or magic-link sign-in, sign-up, or password reset screens.
whenNotToUse: Material Design 3 apps: the MD3 sign-in is the login example (get_example login) built from md3-* components.
Single sign-on only: a card with one provider Button is enough.

children.role: variant=destructive, only after a failed sign-in
variant=link asChild around <a href>: Forgot password?
type=submit variant=cta, full width, disabled while pending
variant=link asChild around <a href>: Create an account

layout: One card, max-w-sm, centered vertically and horizontally; nothing else competes on the page.
Field order matches the autofill order: email, then password.
The submit Button spans the card width; secondary paths are links: Button variant="link" asChild around an <a href>, not buttons.
responsive: The card is full width with px-4 page padding on phones and max-w-sm from there; no layout change is needed.
accessibility: The card title is the page's h1 (CardTitle renders h3: pass role=heading aria-level={1} or wrap your own h1).
Every Input has a Label htmlFor; required fields use Label required.
Errors: Input invalid + a text message linked with aria-describedby; the form-level Alert has role=alert.
Use type=email/password and autoComplete so password managers work.
Don't disable the submit button for invalid input; validate on submit and explain.
patterns.states: Pending: disable submit and change its label ("Signing in…"). Failure: destructive Alert, keep the inputs. Success: navigate away; no success message on this page.
antiPatterns: Placeholder text as the only label.
Clearing the password field's neighbours on a failed attempt.
Raw <a> or <button> styled by hand for secondary links: use link Button (variant="link" asChild).

patterns.name: Dashboard overview
patterns.summary: KPI metric cards, a progress panel and a recent-activity table in a responsive card grid.
patterns.description: The home page of a SaaS or admin app: what matters right now at a glance. Every region is a CardContainer so regions can be added, removed or reordered without changing the grid.
whenToUse: Users need a summary of several metrics and recent changes before drilling in.
whenNotToUse: Charting-heavy analytics: Nucleux ships @nucleux/chart (ChartContainer, ChartTooltip, ChartLegend over Recharts) — check get_component chart and add chart cards to this grid rather than a separate layout.
A page with one dominant task (use list-page or a form).

children.role: Page header: <h1> title + muted description, flex-col sm:flex-row
MetricCard: label, large tabular value, change line

layout: 4 KPIs maximum in the top row; more belong on an analytics page.
Use tabular-nums for metric values so digits align.
Every region is a card with a CardTitle; no free-floating content between cards.
responsive: KPI row: 1 column, sm:grid-cols-2, xl:grid-cols-4.
Detail grid: stacked below lg, lg:grid-cols-3 with the table spanning 2.
Hide low-priority table columns below sm (hidden sm:table-cell) and wrap tables in overflow-x-auto.
accessibility: CardTitle renders an <h3>. Directly under the page's <h1> pass aria-level={2} so the heading order does not skip a level.
Label the KPI section (aria-label="Key metrics").
Decorative metric icons get aria-hidden.
Every Progress needs an aria-label naming what it measures.
patterns.states: While data loads render Skeleton blocks in each card at the same size; on failure show Empty inside the affected card only, so the rest of the dashboard stays usable.
antiPatterns: Raw hex colors for trend arrows: use text-success / text-destructive tokens.
Hand-built progress bars with divs instead of Progress.

patterns.name: Record detail page
patterns.summary: Breadcrumb back to the list, header with status badge and actions, tabbed sections of facts in cards, and a confirmation dialog before delete.
patterns.description: The page for one record (a project, user, order, booking). It answers "what is this and what can I do with it": identity and status in the header, the record's actions next to the title, details grouped into tabs, and destructive actions guarded by AlertDialog.
whenToUse: Users open one record from a list to see everything about it and act on it.
whenNotToUse: Quick edits of a few fields: use form-dialog from the list page.
Records with one field group: skip Tabs and show the cards directly.

children.role: Page header: <h1> title + muted description, flex-col sm:flex-row; title = record name; badges = status; actions = Edit (secondary) + Delete (destructive)
Facts as a <dl>, 2 columns from sm
destructive confirmation; names the record and the consequence

layout: Facts are a description list (dl/dt/dd), not a table and not loose paragraphs.
Record actions live in the page header's actions: secondary for edit, destructive for delete; at most one cta.
Tabs only when there are two or more sections; the first tab is the overview.
responsive: The header stacks actions under the title below sm (flex-col sm:flex-row).
Overview grid stacks below lg; facts go from 1 to 2 columns at sm.
accessibility: Breadcrumb's current item is BreadcrumbPage (aria-current) and not a link.
CardTitle renders h3; under the page's <h1> pass aria-level={2}.
AlertDialog title names the record ("Delete \"Website redesign\"?") and the description states what is lost; the confirm label repeats the verb.
patterns.states: Loading: page-states skeleton in the content area, keeping breadcrumb and title placeholders. Not found: Empty with a link back to the list.
antiPatterns: Delete without confirmation.
window.confirm for confirmations.
A generic "Are you sure?" that does not name the record.

patterns.name: Create/edit form in a dialog
patterns.summary: Dialog with a labelled form, validation on submit, Cancel + one primary action, and a success toast. One component handles create and edit.
patterns.description: For creating or editing a record without leaving the page it belongs to (new task from a board, edit member from a team list). Up to ~6 fields; longer flows belong on their own page or in multi-step-form.
whenToUse: A short form (≤ 6 fields) started from a list, board or detail page.
whenNotToUse: Long or multi-section forms: use a page or multi-step-form.
Confirmations with no input: use AlertDialog.

children.role: noValidate onSubmit; wraps header, fields and footer so Enter submits
Fields, space-y-4; paired short fields in sm:grid-cols-2

composition.role: Once at the app root; call useToast().toast({ variant: "success", title }) after saving

layout: The <form> wraps DialogHeader, fields and DialogFooter so the submit button is inside it.
Footer: Cancel then the primary action, right-aligned.
Reset the draft after a successful save; keep it after a failure.
responsive: Paired fields (priority + due date) are one column on phones, two from sm.
Dialog keeps p-4 inset from the viewport edge; avoid fixed widths larger than max-w-lg.
accessibility: Dialog wires DialogTitle/DialogDescription to aria-labelledby/aria-describedby: always render both.
Each field has a Label htmlFor; DatePicker takes aria-label.
Invalid fields: Input invalid + message via aria-describedby.
patterns.states: Saving: disable the submit button. Failure: destructive Alert inside the dialog, keep input. Success: close and show a toast.
antiPatterns: Submit button outside the <form> (Enter does nothing).
Closing the dialog on failure.
Calling useToast outside ToastProvider (it throws).

patterns.name: Collection list page with search, filter and pagination
patterns.summary: Page header with the primary create action, a search + filter toolbar, and a sortable paginated DataTable.
patterns.description: The standard page for browsing a collection of records (projects, tasks, users, orders, bookings). Filtering runs before the table, so DataTable's built-in sorting and pagination always apply to the filtered rows.
whenToUse: Users scan, search, filter or sort many records of the same shape.
whenNotToUse: Fewer than ~5 items, or items that are visual (use cards in a grid).
Server-side pagination over very large datasets: DataTable paginates client-side; pass one page of data and render Pagination yourself.

composition.role: Page container (mx-auto max-w-6xl, responsive padding, flex-col gap-6)

children.role: Page header: <h1> title + muted description, flex-col sm:flex-row; actions slot holds the primary Button (variant cta)
Toolbar (role=search): stacks on mobile, row from sm
Sortable, paginated rows; Badge in cells for status

layout: One primary action, in the page header's actions. Row actions go in a trailing column (DropdownMenu or ghost Buttons).
Keep filter state in the page (or URL search params) and pass filtered rows to DataTable.
DataTable paginates internally (pageSize, default 10). Use the separate Pagination component only for server-side paging.
responsive: Toolbar: flex-col below sm, flex-row from sm; search Input (type="search") grows (sm:flex-1), filters get fixed widths.
Wrap DataTable in overflow-x-auto so wide tables scroll inside the page instead of the page scrolling sideways.
Keep columns to what fits; drop secondary columns from the columns array on small screens rather than squeezing them.
accessibility: search Input (type="search") and NativeSelect need aria-label when no visible <Label> is rendered.
Wrap the toolbar in role=search.
Communicate status with Badge text, not color alone.
Set emptyMessage to explain an empty filter result.
patterns.states: Loading: render ListSkeleton from page-states in place of the table. Error: Empty with role="alert" with Retry. No records at all (not just no matches): Empty with the create action.
antiPatterns: Rebuilding sorting/pagination by hand around Table when DataTable already does it.
Filtering inside cell renderers instead of before passing data.
Importing ColumnDef from @tanstack/react-table without installing it: type columns as DataTableProps<Row, unknown>["columns"] or add the dependency.

patterns.name: Multi-step form
patterns.summary: One card with a step counter and Progress, one field group per step, per-step validation, Back/Next, and a review step before submit.
patterns.description: Onboarding, setup wizards, checkout and other flows that are too long for one screen. Each step validates before advancing; the last step lists every answer for review.
whenToUse: More than ~6 fields that split into ordered groups.
Later questions depend on earlier answers.
whenNotToUse: Settings users revisit in any order: use settings-page tabs.
Short forms: one card or form-dialog.

children.role: Step N of M (aria-live), Progress, step title
Current step's fields; review step is a <dl>

layout: Keep Back/Next in the same place on every step.
Name the step in the header, and name the final action for what it does ("Create workspace").
Keep answers in one state object so Back never loses input.
responsive: Single column at every width; the card is full width on phones.
accessibility: The step counter is aria-live=polite so screen readers hear the step change.
Move focus to the step title or first field when the step changes in your app.
Progress has an aria-label.
patterns.states: Final submit pending: disable both buttons. Failure: Alert on the review step with the answers intact.
antiPatterns: Validating every step only at the end.
Discarding later answers when going Back.
Using AgentSteps for form steps: it is for showing an AI agent's progress.

patterns.name: Loading, empty and error states
patterns.summary: One AsyncContent wrapper that renders a skeleton, a recoverable error, an empty state with an action, or the content.
patterns.description: Every page or card that loads data needs all four states. Skeleton mirrors the content's shape while loading; Empty covers both failures (role=alert, destructive media tint, with Retry) and empty collections (with the create action).
whenToUse: Any view backed by async data.
whenNotToUse: Inline field validation (use Input invalid + Alert in forms).
Transient success/failure notices after an action (use Toast).

composition.role: App-level helper (in the example) switching on a LoadState union

children.role: error: role=alert, EmptyMedia with bg-destructive/10 text-destructive, Retry Button in EmptyContent
empty: EmptyMedia variant=icon, primary create Button in EmptyContent

layout: Render states in the same box the content will occupy, so the page does not jump.
Distinguish "no records yet" (empty state + create action) from "no matches" (DataTable emptyMessage + clear filters).
responsive: Empty is centered and width-agnostic; Skeleton rows should use the same responsive grid as the content.
accessibility: Loading container: role=status aria-live=polite with a visually hidden "Loading…".
Error container: role=alert so the failure is announced.
Retry is a real Button that re-runs the request; keep the user's filters and input.
antiPatterns: A full-page spinner for a partial reload.
Blank screens when a list is empty.
Error text with no recovery action.

patterns.name: Settings and profile page
patterns.summary: Tabbed settings with card sections: a profile form that saves explicitly and toggle rows that apply instantly.
patterns.description: Account, profile, notification and workspace preferences. Tabs group sections; each section is a card. Text fields are a form with a Save button and a success Alert; switches take effect immediately.
whenToUse: Users change preferences or profile fields.
whenNotToUse: Multi-step setup or onboarding (sequence the steps instead of tabs).
A single toggle (put it where it takes effect).

children.role: Page header: <h1> title + muted description, flex-col sm:flex-row

layout: Settings read best narrow: max-w-3xl.
SettingRow: text on the left, control on the right; one setting per row.
Forms save explicitly (submit Button bottom-right); switches apply immediately and need no Save.
responsive: SettingRow stacks (flex-col) below sm and becomes a row from sm.
With more than 4 tabs, consider orientation="vertical" Tabs on lg or separate routes.
accessibility: CardTitle renders an <h3>. Directly under the page's <h1> pass aria-level={2} so the heading order does not skip a level.
Every Input/NativeSelect has a <Label htmlFor>. Mark required fields with Label required.
Switch is a button: connect it to its visible text with aria-labelledby/aria-describedby (or give it aria-label).
Show validation with Input invalid plus a text hint linked through aria-describedby.
Confirm saves with Alert variant=success; announce errors with Alert variant=destructive.
patterns.states: Disable Save while the form is invalid or submitting; keep user input after a failed save and show a destructive Alert.
antiPatterns: A Save button for switches that already applied.
Placeholder text used as the only label.
Using the deprecated Alert severity prop: use variant.

patterns.name: Task board (kanban)
patterns.summary: Status columns of task cards with priority, due date and assignee; a per-card actions menu (DropdownMenu) moves and deletes tasks without drag and drop.
patterns.description: Kanban-style board for tasks, tickets or pipeline stages. Each card shows the essentials as text; moving a task is a menu action so the board works by keyboard. Includes the menu-button composition (DropdownMenu with an icon Button trigger) for row and card actions anywhere in an app.
whenToUse: Items move through a few ordered statuses and users scan by status.
whenNotToUse: Many items needing sorting/filtering by several fields: use list-page (offer both as a Board/List toggle).
More than ~6 statuses.

composition.role: Board: grid, 1 column on phones, md:grid-cols-2, 2xl:grid-cols-4

children.role: asChild around a ghost Button size=icon-sm; aria-label names the task

layout: Columns stack on phones, pair from md and go four-up only from 2xl: next to an expanded 16rem Sidebar, xl leaves ~230px per column, too narrow for card metadata.
DropdownMenu is not portaled: never put a menu trigger inside an overflow-x/overflow-y container (a horizontally scrolling board, a scroll area) or the menu is clipped.
A card shows title, project, priority Badge, due date, assignee; details open in detail-page or form-dialog.

Menu button: DropdownMenuTrigger asChild wrapping a Button (variant="ghost" size="icon-sm") with an aria-label. DropdownMenuItem onSelect runs the action; the menu closes and focus returns to the trigger.
Show an empty column as a dashed placeholder, not nothing.
responsive: 1 column below md, 2 from md, 4 from 2xl (grid items-start so short columns don't stretch).
Avoid a horizontally scrolling board: it clips the card menus (see Layout).
accessibility: Each column is a section labelled by its heading; card titles are h3.
Moving and deleting are menu items, so no drag and drop is required (add drag as an enhancement only).
DropdownMenu has role=menu/menuitem with arrow-key, Home/End and Escape handling; the trigger's aria-label says whose actions it opens.
patterns.states: Loading: three Skeleton cards per column. Empty board: Empty with a create action.
antiPatterns: Drag and drop as the only way to change status.
Nesting a Button inside DropdownMenuTrigger without asChild (button inside button).
Status shown only by card color.
